> When set to "Mode -> canvas layer" and "Aspect ->expand", no black bars should appear and the game should be stretched to cover the sides, but in Beta1 this stretching doesn't happen.

This is done by design by default, following https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101807. You have to use the buttons on the top to change the viewport size.

I don't think there's a perfect solution here. Either we revert to the 4.4.beta1 behavior which [many](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101691) [people](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101759) [found confusing](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102082) ([myself included](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100883)), or we keep the current behavior which ensures you see the same visual result as a non-embedded window by default, but won't resize as you increase the window size until you use the buttons at the top.

I find this confusing, as now it is needed to change to the 3rd option to test the "stretch" project settings which is not intuitive.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73e9171c-79e2-4646-bd8d-c421f44399bb)

Am I correct to say that only with this 3rd option all display project settings will have effect on the window (that includes stretch settings)? if yes, I think this should be the default.
Also, this option has the same behavior as 4.3 and before, so it makes sense to me to have it as default

> Am I correct to say that only with this 3rd option all display project settings will have effect on the window (that includes stretch settings)?

Yes.

> if yes, I think this should be the default.

The problem with making this the default is that the default floating window size does not match the project's default viewport size (or window size override) defined in the project settings. This is because the floating window will be preserved across runs (so the user can resize it to have a different size), but also because the window size doesn't take into account the chrome[^1] around the game viewport. In short, it's why a 1920x1080 window cannot fit a 1920x1080 game viewport, but a slightly smaller one instead.

If we were to use the game viewport dimensions by default, we'd have to make it not preserve the window position/size across restarts, which many people would find to be a downgrade. We'd also have to resize resize the window to take the chrome size into account, which is possible but likely finnicky when your game viewport size is just a little bit smaller than your display size (as you won't have enough space to expand the window).

[^1]: The "chrome" refers to the floating window's buttons here.

> Also, this option has the same behavior as 4.3 and before, so it makes sense to me to have it as default

There's a proposal about disabling game window embedding by default, which would fully restore 4.3 behavior by default: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11677

I understand, still from my point of view, it is the most intuitive for me to have the game window to respect all display settings by default, and change the option if you want it to match the default viewport size, not vice-versa. I think specially for beginners since it it not obvious right now why the stretch options are not taking effect. I'm a Godot junior so probably I'm missing some special cases, but this is my grain of salt to the matter.

If no change is done, I think it would be necessary to document the need to change the game window option in order to see the display settings taking effect, maybe in the stretch settings themselves? Altough this feels clunky, but else I think this will cause headaches to begginers

Just for information, since #101807 the window size is always using the project and editor settings on game run. Even if the user resizes the window, next start, it will respect the settings. This was an adjustment following multiple issues linked to the non respect of the project/editor settings and it is closer to the non embedded behaviour.

I agree more and more that the embedding should be disabled by default following multiple issues and comments, at least until it's more stable/easier to use/understood/better documented. It's actually to different from the behaviour that users are used to.

That being said, I also saw a lot of great comments about the embedding in the editor!

I concur that the current behavior is not optimal. I'd expect the debug window to function as similarly as possible to how the real game will; otherwise it will be harder to discover and fix game scaling and window management issues.

I don't understand why changing this behavior would require reverting the window memory feature? They don't seem mutually exclusive to me; have the debug window default to the game's settings when opened the first time, and then if the developer makes some change to the debug window, remember that change for future sessions.

(Additionally, it sounds like the memory mostly applies to window size and position, which is separate from scaling mode. I can't think of a common reason why a dev would want to set their scaling mode in the debug window to one other than the game's default scaling mode, so I'm not convinced that that setting even needs to be remembered between sessions at all.)

I'm not familiar with the inner workings here, could easily be missing something, but as far as I can tell it seems possible to have the best of both worlds.
